Prepare for Texas school counselor certification with Texas Tech’s online Master of Education in School Counseling. This 48-credit-hour graduate program integrates counseling theory, ethical practice, diversity, assessment and supervised practicum experience in K–12 settings.

Texas Tech University’s Online Master of Education in School Counseling is a 48-credit-hour graduate program designed to prepare candidates for Texas school counselor certification. The curriculum integrates counseling theory, ethical and legal foundations, diversity, career development, assessment, crisis intervention, and child and adolescent counseling. Students build competencies in individual and group counseling, family systems, addiction awareness and culturally responsive practice. TEA-aligned coursework is paired with a supervised practicum experience that provides hands-on application in school settings under professional supervision. The program emphasizes ethical decision-making, data-informed program management and the development of comprehensive school counseling programs aligned with state and district goals. Graduates are prepared to promote academic achievement, career readiness and social-emotional development while meeting Texas certification requirements and serving effectively in elementary, middle and high school environments.

Please plan to submit the following with your application:

**Industry Career Certificates at Texas Tech Online**

**Overview**
- Industry Career Certificates are online, in-demand, self-paced professional certificates offered through Coursera Career Academy.
- These certificates are provided at no cost to TTU students, faculty, and staff as optional, non-credit enhancements to your degree.
- Certificates are created by industry leaders such as Google, IBM, Meta, and HubSpot.
- They are designed to help you gain job-ready skills, explore new career paths, and stand out in the job market.

**Eligibility**
- Available to Texas Tech University students, faculty, and staff with a TTU email address.
- First-year, first-semester students receive invitations at the start of their second semester.
- Not recommended for students currently on academic probation.
- Alumni access is in development—updates will be provided as available.

**Key Features**
- Self-paced and on-demand: Complete certificates at your own speed.
- No cost: Free for eligible TTU participants.
- Non-credit: These do not count toward your degree requirements.
- No limit: You can complete as many certificates as you wish.
- Receive a digital certificate upon completion (some courses may require name or identity verification).

**Popular Certificate Providers**
- Google
- IBM
- Meta
- HubSpot

**How to Enroll**
1. Visit the [Industry Career Certificates info page](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/careercertificates/info/).
2. Sign up using your Texas Tech University email address.
3. Follow the instructions to enroll in your chosen certificate(s).

**Support & Troubleshooting**
- For technical issues or account linking, visit [Coursera Learner Support](https://learner.coursera.help/hc).
- For TTU-specific questions or if you cannot access a desired certificate, email: online.careercertificates@ttu.edu or call 806.742.4049.

**Additional Information**
- Certificates are optional and do not replace credit-bearing courses.
- You may reset deadlines as needed; there is no penalty for missing suggested deadlines.
- Texas Tech administrators can view your grades and progress in these certificates.

**Next Steps**
- Explore available certificates and enroll: [TTU Industry Career Certificates](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/careercertificates/info/)
- For more details or help, contact online.careercertificates@ttu.edu or 806.742.4049.

answer.text:
**Texas Tech Microcredentials – Overview**

**What Are Microcredentials?**
- Short, targeted programs designed to build specific, in-demand career skills.
- Approved by Texas Tech University, ensuring high quality.
- Flexible formats: online on-demand, hybrid, and face-to-face options.
- Upon completion, you earn a digital badge as proof of your achievement.

**Who Are They For?**
- Current undergraduate and graduate students
- Working professionals seeking to upskill or reskill

**Benefits**
- Fast: Earn a credential in less time than a degree.
- Flexible: Choose from various program lengths and formats.
- Focused: Gain just the skills you need, without a long-term commitment.
- Some microcredentials may offer credit toward a Texas Tech degree.

**Types of Microcredentials Available**

- **Industry Career Certificates** (Available Now)
  - Nearly 40 in-demand certificate programs from Google, Meta, IBM, and more via Coursera Career Academy.
  - Free for Texas Tech undergraduate and graduate students.
  - [Learn more and enroll](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/careercertificates/info/)

- **Texas Tech Faculty-Developed Microcredentials** (Coming Soon)
  - Topics will include communication, business, technology, leadership, finance, and human resources.
  - Designed for non-traditional learners and working professionals.
  - Will offer online, hybrid, and Saturday classes at TTU DFW for some programs.

**Digital Badges**
- Upon completion, receive a digital badge that is Texas Tech University approved.
- Badges are easily shareable with employers and provide a direct link to your accomplishments.

**How to Earn a Microcredential**
- Enroll in the desired microcredential program.
- Complete the required coursework or activities.
- Receive your digital badge upon successful completion.

**More Information & Next Steps**
- Explore current microcredential options: [TTU Industry Career Certificates](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/careercertificates/info/)
- Stay tuned for new Texas Tech faculty-developed microcredentials launching soon!
- For questions, contact TTU Online+ at 1-844-691-0494 or online@ttu.edu.

Let me know if you’d like details about a specific microcredential or how to get started!

Comprehensive Evaluation/Comprehensive Examination

All TTU graduate students MUST complete a comprehensive evaluation in order to graduate. There are four (4) different options for students in the CS Dept. to complete this:

Step 1: Master's Thesis

Step 2: Students must publicly defend their completed thesis to satisfy this requirement. Six (6) hours of CS 6000 - Master's Thesis AND CS faculty approval is required.

Step 3: Master's Project

Step 4: Students will complete an oral examination wherein they present publicly on project results. Requires three (3) credit hours of CS 6001 - Master's Project AND CS faculty approval

Step 5: Industry Career Certificate through Coursera

Step 6: Students will complete an approved industry career certificate through Coursera. Students can begin the certificate of their choice from the CS Learning Program as early as their first semester in the program.

Step 7: Work Experience

Step 8: Students can participate in an approved internship/CPT (see grad advisor). The internship/CPT requires co-enrollment in CS 5000 - Practicum in Computer Science

Step 9: Distance students who are working full-time professionals in a relevant industry may ask that their full-time job be considered to satisfy this requirement (see grad advisor).

The CS Dept. no longer offers an exam or report option.

If asked questions about the Online Doctor of Education in Agricultural Education, answer with

The joint Ed.D. program (Doc@Distance) previously provided by Texas Tech University and Texas A&M University will not admit a cohort in 2019. This is a result of recent graduate program reviews at both universities and reflection on the future of the program.

If you are interested in pursuing a doctoral graduate degree via distance, you can still do so at Texas Tech University with the Doctor of Education in agricultural education degree program.

The Doctor of Education in agricultural education degree program builds on previous undergraduate and graduate courses along with their life experiences (including three years of related work experiences). It is designed to develop independent and critical thinking. Emphasis is placed on selecting courses and experiences that lead to a thorough and comprehensive knowledge of agricultural education and/or agricultural communications, a supporting field, and methods of research and statistics.

Step 1: This degree program requires a minimum of 72 semester hours of graduate coursework beyond the baccalaureate degree along with the development of a dissertation.

Step 2: At or near the end of coursework, the student will take a qualifying written examination consisting of eight hours for Agricultural Education, four hours for Research, Evaluation, and Statistics; and four hours for the Supporting Field.

Step 3: No more than one week after the written examination, the student will take an oral qualifying examination. Both of these examinations will be administered by the student's advisory committee (consisting of at least three members of the graduate faculty).

Step 4: After completion of the dissertation, the student will present and defend a dissertation.

Please note that this program is offered by main campus and is 100% Online - Asynchronous

Learner Guide

A short help document provided by Texas Tech that explains how to enroll, link accounts, use the Industry Career Certificates program, and where to get help.

Learner support team

Coursera’s help team who assist with account linking, verification, access problems, and other issues related to Coursera courses and certificates.

Learning history

A record of courses, progress, and certificates associated with a user account on a learning platform.

Learning program / learner program

A group or collection of courses or certificates an organization (like TTU) provides to its learners through Coursera.

My Coursera

The personal view of the Coursera consumer site. If you see “My Coursera,” you are on the public Coursera site (not the organization-sponsored program) and may be asked to pay for content.

Name verification

A check to confirm a learner’s real name. If name verification is pending, certificate issuance may be delayed until the learner completes the verification steps.

What degree will I earn?

The 10K Degree Completion Program offers a swift and cost-effective route to obtaining a Bachelor of Science in Leadership Studies or a Bachelor of Arts in University Studies. We recognize that each student is unique, which is why we offer a diverse array of options to customize their educational journey according to their passions and professional aspirations. Our flexible and dynamic pathway enables the utilization of transfer credits that might otherwise remain unused in alternative majors.

Our core curriculum is meticulously crafted for interdisciplinary students, fostering the development of knowledge, skills, and abilities to address global concerns, solve complex problems, and engage with contemporary social issues from multiple perspectives.

Increase Your Earning Potential with a Flexible, Accelerated Bachelor's Degree Program

On average, graduates with a bachelor's degree earn $22,000 more per year than high school graduates, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. The Interdisciplinary Studies program offers a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree, that provides students with a diverse range of options to tailor their education to their interests and career goals.

The Leadership Studies Bachelor of Science (BS) degree further enhances this advantage by offering a dynamic and customizable pathway. Our core curriculum is meticulously crafted for interdisciplinary students, fostering the development of knowledge, skills, and abilities to address global concerns, solve complex problems, and engage with contemporary social issues from multiple perspectives.

Graduates of our $10K Degree Completion Program possess the tools and skills for success across various fields, including business, education, government, computing applications, healthcare, and more. We understand that students pursuing degrees in general studies require unique career paths, necessitating a program of study that offers flexibility. With Texas Tech's flexible, accelerated bachelor's degree, you can fully explore and integrate customizable areas of study, ensuring that your education aligns seamlessly with your career goals and future plans. Join us in embracing adaptability and unlocking a broad skill set that positions you for success in today's dynamic job market.

The $10K Degree Completion Program is Designed to help Adult Learners Level Up

It's never too late to chase your dream of earning a degree. With our hybrid and online courses specifically designed for returning learners, you can easily manage school alongside your other commitments. Invest in your future and that of your family by embracing the numerous advantages that come with a TTU degree. Our program is crafted to support adult learners and working professionals as they progress toward completing their bachelor's degree.

Texas Tech University's Bachelor of Science in Kinesiology program—available fully online or in a hybrid format on campus in Lubbock—equips you for diverse health-related careers. Gain the knowledge and skills to make a meaningful impact on health and well-being.

Advance your career in health, fitness and human movement with Texas Tech University's Bachelor of Science in Kinesiology—available fully online or in a hybrid format on campus in Lubbock. This flexible program is designed for students interested in the science of human movement, exercise and wellness, preparing them for careers in health, fitness, rehabilitation, and beyond. Build a strong foundation in exercise science, nutrition for exercise and performance, biomechanics, applied exercise physiology and exercise testing and prescription. The curriculum is tailored to provide industry-relevant skills that set you apart in the job market, while also preparing you for advanced studies and careers in physical therapy, occupational therapy, strength and conditioning, cardiac rehabilitation and other health-related fields.

KIN 4306 - Exercise Testing and Prescription

Study of the recommended procedures for exercise testing and prescription for healthy adults and people with chronic disease. The course emphasizes the practical application of standard guidelines used by exercise professionals when screening, evaluating risk, assessing health and fitness, and designing exercise programs.

The course covers various bodily systems and how they work together to maintain a stable internal environment during exercise. KIN 3306 - Applied Exercise Physiology

Examination of how the human body adapts to different internal and external stressors. The course will study bodily adaptations to exercise training as well as exposure to environmental stress including heat, cold, and altitude. Factors that affect exercise performance will also be discussed including ergogenic aids and special populations.

KIN 3347 - Nutrition for Exercise and Performance

This course covers key nutrition recommendations for active individuals, including optimal intakes of macronutrients (carbohydrates, fats, and proteins) and micronutrients (vitamins and minerals). It also includes a critical examination of dietary supplement strategies to improve exercise performance, as well as consideration of current topics in sports nutrition, such as nutrient timing, meal frequency, and the influence of nutrition on body composition.

- Review your schedule in Raiderlink to ensure your courses are correctly registered.

Prepare for leadership roles in colleges and universities with Texas Tech’s fully online Master of Education in Higher Education Administration. This 30-credit-hour program builds expertise in student development, institutional leadership, assessment and strategic administration.

Texas Tech University’s Online Master of Education in Higher Education Administration is a 30-credit-hour graduate program designed to prepare professionals for leadership roles across postsecondary institutions. Delivered fully online in an asynchronous format, the program integrates theory and applied practice in student affairs, institutional administration, budgeting, crisis management and higher education policy. Students examine the historical foundations of American higher education while developing practical competencies in assessment, student development, organizational leadership and strategic decision-making. Coursework emphasizes ethical leadership, resource management and data-informed planning within complex institutional environments. The program culminates in a capstone experience that synthesizes leadership theory with applied administrative practice. Graduates are prepared to advance institutional effectiveness and student success in colleges, universities and community colleges through roles that require strategic insight, operational expertise and collaborative leadership.

Bachelor's degree from any accredited institution. No GMAT/GRE is required.

Curriculum

The curriculum for the Master of Engineering program consists of 30 semester credit hours of coordinated graduate level course work. No more than 12 credit hours (4 courses) can be taken in any single engineering discipline, e.g., Industrial Engineering or Mechanical Engineering.

The program allows up to six hours of course work to be taken outside of engineering, upon the approval of the graduate advisor.

Every candidate for a master's degree is required to pass a final comprehensive examination.In the final semester, students must take the Master’s report course (ENGR6330) which serves as their comprehensive exam requirement for graduation.

Transfer of Courses

Students may be permitted to transfer up to six credit hours of relevant engineering coursework from another university graduate program upon approval of the Graduate School. All transfer courses are subject to the same time limitations as courses taken in the program (a maximum of six years from the first course in the plan of study until graduation).

Bachelor's degree from any accredited institution. No GMAT/GRE is required.
